subject: ventures/med-spa-treatment-profit-calculator
professional: a med spa business consultant / practice CFO who prices injectables and device treatments and builds per-treatment contribution models; first check: that cost per visit includes product, card fees, provider and room time, and that thousands-formatted prices ($1,200) are read correctly

evidence.correctness: Ran analyse() on a 3-treatment menu (Botox 450/160/30min/40, Filler 900/350/45/20, Hydrafacial 200/40/60/30; provider $60/h, room $40/h, 10 min turnover, 3% fee, 50% target, 200 room hours, $8000 fixed) and recomputed independently in Python. Matched exactly: contribution/visit 219.83, 441.33, 47.33; per room hour 329.75, 481.45, 40.57; break-even price 223.37, 445.02, 151.2; target price 460.99, 918.44, 312.06; monthly contribution 19040, profit 11040, room hours 80, break-even room hours 33.61. The Python check was written by me from the same formulas (no external standard exists), so it confirms the arithmetic, not the model. Page not loaded in a browser (none available); page.test.mjs ran. Capped at 2 because input handling gives silently wrong numbers: 'Filler,1,200,300,60,10' (a $1,200 price typed with a thousands comma) is accepted as price 1, product 200, minutes 300, volume 60, the 5th field dropped, yielding contribution -705.70 with no warning.
evidence.completeness: Checked each README claim by running it: parseTreatments (comma/tab, header skip, bad lines reported for too-few-fields and non-numeric), treatmentEconomics (contribution, margin, per room hour, break-even, target price), analyse (monthly mix, capacity check, fixed-cost check, findings) all work end to end. llms.txt, sitemap, robots, usage.mjs, disclaimer present. Stage is 'prototype' in VENTURE.yaml. One README claim ('bad lines are reported, never dropped') is false for lines with more than 5 fields. No TODO stubs found.
evidence.verification: cd ventures/med-spa-treatment-profit-calculator && node --test '*.test.mjs': 25 pass, 0 fail. Mutation 1: room cost charged for treatment minutes only (dropping turnover) in treatmentEconomics: 1 test failed (caught). Mutation 2: removed the fee term from the target-price denominator: 2 tests failed (caught). Both reverted with git checkout; git status clean. Tests are the author's own expectations and have no case for thousands separators or extra fields.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (113 lines), skimmed index.html and tests. Clean pure functions, no dependencies, input coerced through nn() so negatives/NaN become 0. Defects: parseTreatments ignores fields beyond the 5th and splits on every comma so '1,200' misparses silently; nn() silently turns negative provider/room/fee inputs into 0 without a finding; feePct silently clamped to 99; targetPrice returns null with no finding when fee plus target margin is 100% or more; margin uses unrounded contribution but displayed contribution is rounded (minor).
evidence.claims: Backed: free/client-side/nothing uploaded (no network code in calc.mjs; usage.mjs only counts), disclaimer text on page and in FAQ, not medical advice, modelling choices listed in findings and README limits. Not backed: FAQ and JSON-LD say injectables 'often land around 40 to 55 percent contribution margin' with no source; README says bad lines are 'never dropped' but extra-field lines are silently truncated.
evidence.fitness: Walked an owner pricing Botox/filler/facial from a pasted menu: the example loads, ranking by profit per room hour and target price answer the job. A real menu pasted from a spreadsheet with $1,200 or '1,200' priced cells breaks silently, and there is no per-unit (per Botox unit) pricing, no consult/no-show/membership modelling (stated as limits), and no tiered provider commission.
evidence.domain: Compared with standard contribution-margin and constrained-resource (profit per scarce hour) practice: variable-cost contribution, ranking by contribution per bottleneck hour, and treating room overhead per occupied hour including turnover is the textbook approach and sensible for med spas. Departures: provider cost charged as a flat loaded hourly rate even when paid on commission; room overhead is a fixed cost allocated as variable, so 'contribution' is a fully-loaded margin, and the fixed-cost line then counts only the separately entered fixed costs (risk of double counting if the user also puts rent in the room rate; not warned).

defects.what: Thousands-formatted price like 1,200 splits on the comma; extra fields are silently dropped and the remaining fields shift, producing a confident wrong result (e.g. price $1, contribution -$705.70) with no 'line not read' warning
FAQ and structured data state an unsourced 40 to 55 percent injectable margin benchmark
Possible double counting of rent between room rate and fixed costs is not warned about
Negative inputs coerced to 0 and fee clamped to 99 without telling the user; targetPrice null gives no finding

verdict: The arithmetic is right and the model (contribution per occupied room hour, target-margin price) is what a med spa consultant would use; 25 tests pass and two seeded mutations were caught. It does not meet the bar because a very common input form, a price with a thousands comma, is silently misread into a wrong, confident result (violating the README's own 'never dropped' claim), and the page carries an unsourced margin benchmark. Finished as a prototype (completeness 3) but correctness and claims are 2.
